claim: If the assessor increases real property value, the taxpayer has 30 calendar days from the notice mailing date to file a written protest with the county assessor.
A protest where the valuation did not change may be filed on or before the first Monday in April.

The assessor issues a written decision within 7 calendar days of the informal hearing; the taxpayer then has 15 calendar days from mailing of the decision to appeal to the county board of equalization.
The taxpayer must file the Section 2835 form with the protest; if not filed, a presumption favors the assessor's valuation in any appeal.

Appeal from the county board of equalization goes to district court (Court of Tax Review if fair cash value exceeds $3,000,000); notice of appeal is due within 30 calendar days of the board order being mailed; trial is de novo.
Full taxes must be paid when due during an appeal; a pending appeal abates and is dismissed if taxes are delinquent and unpaid.
Statewide assessment level for locally valued property is a minimum of 11% and maximum of 13.5% for each real property subclass (10%-15% for personal property).
cite: 2024 Ad Valorem Statistics Book, Oklahoma Tax Commission

Each homestead is exempt from ad valorem taxation to the extent of $1,000 of assessed valuation.
An additional $1,000 assessed-valuation exemption applies for heads of households whose gross household income for the preceding calendar year did not exceed $30,000.

The exemption is granted for a tax year only if the application is filed with the county assessor by March 15 (or within 30 days after a valuation increase notice, whichever is later); later applications take effect the following tax year.
A taxpayer granted a homestead exemption who continues to occupy the home as a homestead need not reapply.
Homestead means the actual residence of a natural person who is a citizen of this state and holds record ownership; only one homestead exemption in the state is allowed per person or family.

Application for the limit on fair cash value of a homestead (Art. X, Sec. 8C) is due by March 15 or within 30 days after a valuation increase notice, whichever is later; no annual reapplication once qualified.

Oklahoma imposes a documentary stamp tax on deeds conveying realty sold when consideration exceeds $100.
Rate is $0.75 for each $500 of consideration or fractional part.
Consideration excludes liens or encumbrances remaining on the property at the time of sale, and includes assumed indebtedness.
The tax is paid by the person who makes, signs, issues or sells the instrument, or for whose use or benefit it is made; stamps must be affixed before the deed is accepted for recording.
The buyer's name and address must appear on the face of the deed before recording.

Exemptions include deeds securing a debt, tax deeds, deeds between spouses or related persons within the second degree without actual consideration, and deeds to a mortgage holder in a qualifying foreclosure.
The OREC form contract allocates documentary stamps to the Seller (Buyer pays Buyer's closing and recording fees).
